## They selected
- shape: box "Check the map's shape"

## Their question
"how do you deterministically check if its well formed or malformed ?"

## How to answer
- `concept`: 2–4 plain sentences, no jargon. `how`: the mechanism; define any term you use. `code`: function names, files and lines.
- `refs`: ids of the boxes, arrows and absences your answer relies on.
- If the map doesn't cover it, explore, then put what you found in `add` (new areas, nodes, edges or absences with evidence, same rules as the map; ids must be new). Connect new boxes to existing ones with arrows where the code really connects them.
- `moves`: `focus` on the most relevant id; `highlight` the ids that make up the path that answers the question.
- If they ask for a change, don't edit (you can't). Propose a `fix`: codemap shows it to them on the map, and if they approve, codemap applies exactly your edits and re-checks the map. So describe it as a proposal waiting for their approval, never as something for them to apply by hand.
- The `fix`: `summary` in plain words; `edits` as exact replacements (`find` copied exactly from the file, occurring once; `replace` is the new text); `creates` for new files. If the fix creates a connection between two boxes, fill `connects` with `from`, `to`, a short `label`, and `evidenceFile` + `evidenceText` (text that will appear in the new code). Keep fixes small and in the style of the surrounding code.
- `followUps`: up to 3 short next questions.

## Evidence rules (a program checks every claim; anything it can't confirm is shown as unconfirmed)
- Every box and arrow cites at least one line: `file` (repo-relative), `line` (1-based), and `text` copied exactly from that line. A distinctive fragment of 10–80 characters works best.
- A box that is a function or method gets `symbol`: "<file>#<name>" (methods as Class.method, object members as obj.member, e.g. "src/db.ts#db.update").
- Arrow `kind`: `calls` when a function in the from box literally calls the function in the to box; `request` when an HTTP call in the from box hits a route handled by the to box; `imports`; `then` for anything else (events, ordering). The checker verifies calls, request and imports against the code, so use them only when literally true.
- Never cite or read secret files (.env, keys).

96	export function isSafeRelativePath(path: string): boolean {
97	  if (!path || path.startsWith('/') || path.includes('\\') || /^[A-Za-z]:/.test(path)) return false;

102	export function parseMap(input: unknown): ParseResult {
103	  const parsed = CodeMap.safeParse(input);
104	  if (!parsed.success) {
105	    return { ok: false, problems: parsed.error.issues.map((i) => `${i.path.join('.') || '(map)'}: ${i.message}`) };
106	  }
107	  const map = parsed.data;
108	  const problems: string[] = [];
109	  const ids = (kind: string, items: readonly { id: string }[]) => {
110	    const seen = new Set<string>();
111	    for (const { id } of items) {
112	      if (seen.has(id)) problems.push(`${kind} id "${id}" is used twice`);
113	      seen.add(id);
114	    }
115	    return seen;
116	  };
117	  const areas = ids('area', map.areas);
118	  const nodes = ids('node', map.nodes);
119	  const edges = ids('edge', map.edges);
120	  const absences = ids('absence', map.absences);
121	  ids('tour stop', map.tour);
122	
123	  const evidence = (where: string, list: readonly Evidence[]) => {
124	    for (const e of list) if (!isSafeRelativePath(e.file)) problems.push(`${where}: evidence file "${e.file}" must be a path inside the repo`);
125	  };
126	  for (const n of map.nodes) {
127	    if (!areas.has(n.area)) problems.push(`node "${n.id}": unknown area "${n.area}"`);
128	    if (n.symbol && !isSafeRelativePath(n.symbol.slice(0, n.symbol.indexOf('#')))) problems.push(`node "${n.id}": symbol file must be a path inside the repo`);
129	    evidence(`node "${n.id}"`, n.evidence);
130	  }
131	  for (const e of map.edges) {
132	    if (!nodes.has(e.from)) problems.push(`edge "${e.id}": unknown node "${e.from}"`);
133	    if (!nodes.has(e.to)) problems.push(`edge "${e.id}": unknown node "${e.to}"`);
134	    evidence(`edge "${e.id}"`, e.evidence);
135	  }
136	  for (const a of map.absences) {
137	    if (a.between && !nodes.has(a.between.from)) problems.push(`absence "${a.id}": unknown node "${a.between.from}"`);
138	    if (a.between && !nodes.has(a.between.to)) problems.push(`absence "${a.id}": unknown node "${a.between.to}"`);
139	  }
140	  for (const t of map.tour) {
141	    const refs: [string, readonly string[] | undefined, Set<string>][] = [
142	      ['area', t.focus.areas, areas], ['node', t.focus.nodes, nodes], ['edge', t.focus.edges, edges], ['absence', t.focus.absences, absences],

The checker confirmed every claim in the map.

## They selected nothing (the question is about the whole map)

## Their question
"how does claude explore or know what to explore ? Is this self-directed by cc?"

## How to answer
- `concept`: 2–4 plain sentences, no jargon. `how`: the mechanism; define any term you use. `code`: function names, files and lines.
- `refs`: ids of the boxes, arrows and absences your answer relies on.
- If the map doesn't cover it, explore, then put what you found in `add` (new areas, nodes, edges or absences with evidence, same rules as the map; ids must be new). Connect new boxes to existing ones with arrows where the code really connects them.
- `moves`: `focus` on the most relevant id; `highlight` the ids that make up the path that answers the question.
- If they ask for a change, don't edit (you can't). Propose a `fix`: codemap shows it to them on the map, and if they approve, codemap applies exactly your edits and re-checks the map. So describe it as a proposal waiting for their approval, never as something for them to apply by hand.
- The `fix`: `summary` in plain words; `edits` as exact replacements (`find` copied exactly from the file, occurring once; `replace` is the new text); `creates` for new files. If the fix creates a connection between two boxes, fill `connects` with `from`, `to`, a short `label`, and `evidenceFile` + `evidenceText` (text that will appear in the new code). Keep fixes small and in the style of the surrounding code.
- `followUps`: up to 3 short next questions.

## Evidence rules (a program checks every claim; anything it can't confirm is shown as unconfirmed)
- Every box and arrow cites at least one line: `file` (repo-relative), `line` (1-based), and `text` copied exactly from that line. A distinctive fragment of 10–80 characters works best.
- A box that is a function or method gets `symbol`: "<file>#<name>" (methods as Class.method, object members as obj.member, e.g. "src/db.ts#db.update").
- Arrow `kind`: `calls` when a function in the from box literally calls the function in the to box; `request` when an HTTP call in the from box hits a route handled by the to box; `imports`; `then` for anything else (events, ordering). The checker verifies calls, request and imports against the code, so use them only when literally true.
- Never cite or read secret files (.env, keys).

1	// The one place codemap talks to a model: a read-only Claude Agent SDK session that returns structured output.
2	// Read, Grep and Glob only; secret files are refused and left out of searches. Tests swap in a fake `Agent`.
3	import * as path from 'node:path';
4	import { query, type HookCallback, type PreToolUseHookInput } from '@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk';
5	import { isSecretPath } from '@codemap/core';
6	
7	export type Progress = { kind: 'read' | 'search' | 'list'; text: string };
8	
9	export type AgentRequest = {
10	  prompt: string;
11	  schema: Record<string, unknown>;
12	  cwd: string;
13	  /** Continue an earlier session (follow-up questions keep what was already read). */
14	  resume?: string | null;
15	  model?: string;
16	  maxTurns?: number;
17	  onProgress?: (p: Progress) => void;
18	  signal?: AbortSignal;
19	};
20	export type AgentResponse = { output: unknown; sessionId: string | null; cost: number | null };
21	export type Agent = (req: AgentRequest) => Promise<AgentResponse>;
22	
23	export const DEFAULT_MODEL = process.env.CODEMAP_MODEL ?? 'claude-opus-5-5';
24	const READ_ONLY = ['Read', 'Grep', 'Glob'];
25	/** ripgrep glob that leaves secret files out of a search the model didn't scope itself. */
26	const NOT_SECRETS = '!**/{.env,.env.*,*.pem,*.key,*.p12,id_rsa*,id_ed25519*,.npmrc,.netrc}';
27	
28	/** A plain-English progress line for a tool call, with paths relative to the repo. */
29	export function progressOf(name: string, input: Record<string, unknown>, cwd: string): Progress | null {
30	  const rel = (p: unknown) => (typeof p === 'string' ? path.relative(cwd, path.resolve(cwd, p)) || '.' : '');
31	  if (name === 'Read') return { kind: 'read', text: `Reading ${rel(input.file_path)}` };
32	  if (name === 'Grep') return { kind: 'search', text: `Searching for "${String(input.pattern ?? '')}"${input.path ? ` in ${rel(input.path)}` : ''}` };
33	  if (name === 'Glob') return { kind: 'list', text: `Looking for files matching ${String(input.pattern ?? '')}` };
34	  return null;
35	}
36	
37	/** Refuse secret files, and keep repo-wide searches away from them. */
38	export function secretGuard(cwd: string): HookCallback {
39	  return async (input) => {
40	    const i = input as PreToolUseHookInput;
41	    const ti = (i.tool_input ?? {}) as Record<string, unknown>;
42	    const target = typeof ti.file_path === 'string' ? ti.file_path : typeof ti.path === 'string' ? ti.path : null;
43	    const rel = target ? path.relative(cwd, path.resolve(cwd, target)) : null;
44	    if (rel && (rel.startsWith('..') || path.isAbsolute(rel))) {
45	      return { hookSpecificOutput: { hookEventName: 'PreToolUse', permissionDecision: 'deny', permissionDecisionReason: 'Only files inside this repo can be read.' } };
46	    }
47	    if (rel && isSecretPath(rel)) {
48	      return { hookSpecificOutput: { hookEventName: 'PreToolUse', permissionDecision: 'deny', permissionDecisionReason: 'Secret files are never read.' } };
49	    }
50	    if (i.tool_name === 'Grep' && ti.glob === undefined && ti.type === undefined) {
51	      return { hookSpecificOutput: { hookEventName: 'PreToolUse', permissionDecision: 'allow', updatedInput: { ...ti, glob: NOT_SECRETS } } };
52	    }
53	    return {};
54	  };
55	}
56	
57	export const sdkAgent: Agent = async (req) => {
58	  const abortController = new AbortController();
59	  req.signal?.addEventListener('abort', () => abortController.abort(), { once: true });
60	  const q = query({
61	    prompt: req.prompt,
62	    options: {
63	      cwd: req.cwd,
64	      model: req.model ?? DEFAULT_MODEL,
65	      tools: READ_ONLY,
66	      allowedTools: READ_ONLY,
67	      permissionMode: 'dontAsk',
68	      settingSources: [],
69	      strictMcpConfig: true,
70	      outputFormat: { type: 'json_schema', schema: req.schema },
71	      maxTurns: req.maxTurns ?? 60,
72	      abortController,
73	      hooks: { PreToolUse: [{ matcher: 'Read|Grep|Glob', hooks: [secretGuard(req.cwd)] }] },
74	      ...(req.resume ? { resume: req.resume } : {}),
75	    },
76	  });
77	  let sessionId: string | null = null;
78	  for await (const m of q) {
79	    if ('session_id' in m && typeof m.session_id === 'string') sessionId = m.session_id;
80	    if (m.type === 'assistant' && !m.parent_tool_use_id) {
81	      for (const block of m.message.content) {
82	        if (block.type !== 'tool_use') continue;
83	        const p = progressOf(block.name, (block.input ?? {}) as Record<string, unknown>, req.cwd);
84	        if (p) req.onProgress?.(p);
85	      }
86	    }
87	    if (m.type === 'result') {
88	      if (m.subtype !== 'success' || m.structured_output === undefined) {
89	        throw Object.assign(new Error(`Claude stopped before answering (${m.subtype}).`), { cost: m.total_cost_usd });
90	      }
91	      return { output: m.structured_output, sessionId, cost: m.total_cost_usd };
92	    }
93	  }
94	  throw new Error('Claude returned no result.');
95	};

3	import * as fs from 'node:fs';
4	import { findFetchSites, initTreeSitter, matchRoute, scanRepoFacts, type RepoScan } from '@codemap/facts';
5	
6	const MAX_LINES = 40;
7	const section = (title: string, lines: string[]) =>
8	  lines.length ? [`${title}:`, ...lines.slice(0, MAX_LINES), ...(lines.length > MAX_LINES ? [`  …and ${lines.length - MAX_LINES} more`] : []), ''] : [];
9	
10	export async function headStart(root: string): Promise<{ text: string; scan: RepoScan | null }> {
11	  await initTreeSitter();
12	  let scan: RepoScan;
13	  try {
14	    scan = scanRepoFacts(root);
15	  } catch {
16	    return { text: '(The automatic scan could not read this repo; explore it directly.)', scan: null };
17	  }
18	  const facts = Object.values(scan.fileFacts);
19	
20	  const entries = facts.flatMap((f) => f.entries).map((e) => `  - ${e.kind} ${e.label}${e.symbol ? ` → ${e.symbol}` : ` (${e.file})`}`);
21	  const routes = facts.flatMap((f) => f.routes);
22	  const routeLines = routes.map((r) => `  - ${r.method} ${r.path} → ${r.handler ?? r.file}`);
23	
24	  const fetchFiles = facts
25	    .filter((f) => /\.(tsx?|jsx?|mjs|cjs)$/.test(f.path))
26	    .flatMap((f) => {
27	      const source = fs.readFileSync(`${root}/${f.path}`, 'utf8');
28	      return /\bfetch\(|axios|ky\./.test(source) ? [{ path: f.path, source, symbols: f.symbols }] : [];
29	    });
30	  const requests = findFetchSites(fetchFiles).flatMap((site) => {
31	    const m = matchRoute(site, routes);
32	    return m ? [`  - ${site.from} sends ${site.method} ${site.url} → ${m.route.handler ?? m.route.file}`] : [];
33	  });
34	
35	  const writers = new Map<string, Set<string>>();
36	  for (const f of facts) for (const w of f.writes) writers.set(w.table, (writers.get(w.table) ?? new Set()).add(w.symbol ?? f.path));
37	  const tables = [...writers].map(([t, by]) => `  - ${t} ← ${[...by].slice(0, 4).join(', ')}`);
38	
39	  const folders = new Map<string, number>();
40	  for (const f of scan.files) {
41	    const top = f.includes('/') ? f.slice(0, f.indexOf('/')) : '(root)';
42	    folders.set(top, (folders.get(top) ?? 0) + 1);
43	  }
44	  const folderLines = [...folders].sort((a, b) => b[1] - a[1]).map(([d, n]) => `  - ${d}/ (${n} files)`);
45	
46	  const text = [
47	    ...section('Ways in (entry points)', entries),
48	    ...section('Routes and their handlers', routeLines),
49	    ...section('Requests from the code that match a route', requests),
50	    ...section('Tables and what writes them', tables),
51	    ...section('Top-level folders', folderLines),
52	  ].join('\n');
53	  return { text: text || '(The automatic scan found no entry points; explore the repo directly.)', scan };
54	}
